messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Boxplot with box width proportional to number of observations
parts:
It's hard to say without seeing the data your're testing with, but I think it's probably because your code isn't getting called. The length(unique(x)) > 1 is true only when each group of data has multiple x values; if, within each group, all the data has the same x values, then it will evaluate to false, and the width-changing code won't be run.

-Winston

On Fri, Jun 1, 2012 at 8:39 AM, Ying <liuyi...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all,

I was trying to modify geom_boxplot and stat_boxplot a little bit in order for the box width to be proportional to the number of observations. I did the following:

In function 'calculate' in stat_boxplot, changed:
if (length(unique(x)) > 1) width <- diff(range(x)) * 0.9
to
if (length(unique(x)) > 1) width <- length(y)

In function 'reparameterise' in geom_boxplot, changed:
df$width <- df$width %||% 
      params$width %||% (resolution(df$x, FALSE) * 0.9)
to
df$width <- df$width*(resolution(df$x, FALSE) * 0.9)/max(df$width)

However, the box width is still the same... Any ideas what I should do?

Thanks,
Ying

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: geom_linerangeh
parts:
I made a trivial new geom -- a horizontal 'linerange' -- because I
needed it (I wanted to do horizontal lineranges, not error bars (so
geom_errorbarh wouldn't work), and coord_flip() was messing up other
things I wanted).
I am playing around with github, so created a fork and added the file.
People could look at it if they want.

https://github.com/bbolker/ggplot2/blob/dd94ff43a152c95ec7f8b86f0a6df5a6216d8369/R/geom-linerangeh.R

or I could submit a pull request.
This particular version turned out to be trivially easy to do.
I haven't fixed the docs/examples yet ...

Ben Bolker

messages.subject: Re: Boxplot with box width proportional to number of observations
parts:
This is the first time I try to modify ggplot2 functions. Here is what I did:

1) change proto(Geom to proto(ggplot2:::Geom for geom_boxplot; similarly change proto(Stat to proto(ggplot2:::Stat for stat_boxplot.

2) In function 'calculate' in stat_boxplot, change:
if (length(unique(x)) > 1) width <- diff(range(x)) * 0.9 to width <- length(y);

In function 'reparameterise' in geom_boxplot, change:
df$width <- df$width %||%params$width %||% (resolution(df$x, FALSE) * 0.9) to df$width <- df$width*(resolution(df$x, FALSE) * 0.9)/max(df$width);

3) Source 'geom-boxplot.r' and 'stat-boxplot.r';

4) run

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) 
p + geom_boxplot()

Is there anything else I should do other than the above? Thank you very much for your help!

Best,
Ying

On Monday, June 4, 2012 10:17:17 AM UTC-4, Ying wrote:

Well I figured out that actually I needed to change the 'objname' to, say, 'boxplot2'. When calling geom_boxplot, I needed to explicitly specify the stat:
p + geom_boxplot(stat='boxplot2')

-Y

On Sunday, June 3, 2012 6:48:02 PM UTC-4, Ying wrote:
This is the first time I try to modify ggplot2 functions. Here is what I did:

1) change proto(Geom to proto(ggplot2:::Geom for geom_boxplot; similarly change proto(Stat to proto(ggplot2:::Stat for stat_boxplot.

2) In function 'calculate' in stat_boxplot, change:
if (length(unique(x)) > 1) width <- diff(range(x)) * 0.9 to width <- length(y);

In function 'reparameterise' in geom_boxplot, change:
df$width <- df$width %||%params$width %||% (resolution(df$x, FALSE) * 0.9) to df$width <- df$width*(resolution(df$x, FALSE) * 0.9)/max(df$width);

3) Source 'geom-boxplot.r' and 'stat-boxplot.r';

4) run
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) 
p + geom_boxplot()

Is there anything else I should do other than the above? Thank you very much for your help!

Best,
Ying
